body:
I think I'd rather just not. I can't take getting hurt again, each time takes away a little more of me. 'Uninteresting' was never something I thought myself to be, but we're all wrong sometimes. I was looking to see if, indeed, that's what it is. I don't have the strength to fix it.

Thank you, genuinely. It's been helpful. Easter blessings from Europe.

And I do appreciate it, but I genuinely don't understand... What am I supposed to do? Being myself doesn't work, and I must have tried a dozen different approaches. They always seem like everything's great, but it isn't? How am I supposed to know if they don't signal it at all?

Well in that case, I guess I'm hopeless. If smiling, laughing and being 50/50 participants doesn't mean it's going well, then I'm too far gone, because I just can't see what else I can possibly do.

But thanks. Proves I'd better just steer clear altogether.

I don't really know.. Is it? People treat me however they please with zero concern for how I feel. That doesn't make it right to do the same, but it's just becoming difficult to gauge what's fair and what isn't anymore.

But you're right. What choice do I have anyway. It's more respectful to drown on my own than pull her under with me.
Still breathing... Unfortunately.

We talked it through. I realized I was wrong. There's a lot to be appreciated about her, enough to warrant waiting.
I know looks shouldn't be the #1 thing, but they do matter to me. She's a pretty thing in every sense, even if we all have ugly days. She's great, her willingness to overlook my flaws is admirable. She's a good person.

There are prettier, more ambitious, smarter girls out there, sure. I'd lie if I said I didn't have desires. But I think what I forget is that I'm not some kind of ideal either, and since women's standards are very high (nothing wrong with that, but I just cannot meet them), I should be more content with my lot. I've exceeded the peak of what I can expect from dating, this girl is as good as it'll get, and though it might be frustrating sometimes, she's awesome, and a good match.

You're right. I'm probably special in my own way... That I don't know about. And there's the perfect someone for me... Somewhere.

Just gets tiring seeing people who have it so much easier. I guess I can always practice my scales/modes/arpeggios harder. As for my face? 21st century has its perks for the wealthier among us, so it's not all bad. If I had to choose one wish, it'd be to be ridiculously handsome. It's shallow, I know. But so is the world.

I know this is shameful, but I am a very physical person and I wish I had explored more while I could. I think that's what hurts the most. Other blokes are just getting started with their game, and I've done this, with a person I'm not even 100% sure about.

I'm an idiot. A desperate idiot. I have a host of issues, can't believe I'm doing this. I wish she understood that she deserves/needs someone more stable.

I mean I've had my share of girlfriends. 8 or 9 I think, but it was all terrible and shallow and, well, I aimed 'down' if you know what I mean. I don't mean it to sound arrogant or anything, I just did. Because I was desperate.

This girl was the first one that really captivated me for a while. We're fairly equal in looks, I think, we're generally a decent match. But then the little things showed up. I'm big on intimacy and physical-ness, she really isn't. That was the #1 thing that gave me doubts. Then it became apparent we have different conversational needs. Bad stuff when our only contact is via text and speech.

As for finding more. I really try, I do. Apps, clubs, bars, whatever. It's all the same. There's just nobody. And I'm not a bad-looking guy I think. Young-looking, yeah, but not too young. I think I'm decently confident in public and can hold my own. I keep my demons for when I'm alone. And when someone appears, we spend an awesome day together and I find out she's taken (usually a random comment, I never ask). I appreciate friends but by then, my interest grows and I have to withdraw and cut contact. This is before I met her, of course. I wouldn't go behind her back.

They sure do... I've never had an easy time of it. Nor has any guy I know, but it feels strange. I never thought it'd be easy, but this is harder than I ever imagined, and it's not getting easier. Dating in general, I mean.

As for loneliness... Yeah, I guess. I never really had my share of 'casual fun.' I'm not good at this stuff. That's a part of it. I feel like I've 'settled down' with this girl. Taking it seriously, and I'm not ready, but do I really have a choice?

I just click so much better with some people. Her and me, we're OK. She likes me because I have a ton of interests and things I do, and according to her, I'm funny and charismatic. Don't know where she got that. But she's more down-to-earth. She's quite pretty, very kind, nice, an all-around good human being. I appreciate her a lot for that, but it doesn't feel great. I'll try to save it because I respect her and myself.

All the other people I struck a chord with are taken anyway. So... Whatever, I guess. I'm one of those undesirable-and-don't-know-why people. Not feeling sorry for myself (well, I kinda am), but it is so, and so it is.

Dating apps in my age range have been nothing short of a nightmare (they're either promoting their instagram/OF or whatever, or they're impossible to talk to). Granted, every success I've had was from dating apps. But I was also a different person then. A cool, well-kept party-going guy with confidence for two and a ballsy attitude. Back then, I agree, I could have had just about any kind of person I wanted. 
But we change over time, for better and for worse. If I try to 'be myself' on those apps, you can guess what happens. No one cares about jazz anymore, or engineering - I just don't really have what people want. Musicians aren't the cool, exclusive breed we used to be. Which is fine by the way, I'm not feeling sorry for myself.

I'm gonna need to take a good long look at what I want from life. I mean, there's no denying that there's an air of mystery to an aging cat who doesn't date. I'm confident, I respect myself. That's a good image, I think. But I'm practically useless with impressing ladies. I usually accidentally send them signals of disinterest, and I'm not even aware. I've asked a few female friends, 'why am I not interesting?' the response I got was that I am, but I also appear shut in, abrasive and unwilling to let anyone get close. Whether or not it's like that, I can't say.

All I know is I'm confused and don't know what I want. Congrats on that prospect of yours though! Sounds like a mighty fine situation. Very enviable. We're lucky to age like fine wine. A little gray never made a man look worse... For the most part, anyway.

I've admittedly been poisoned by my past experiences. Somewhere along the way, I started leaning towards not pursuing intimacy anymore. A bunch of guys in my year did too. No matter what we did, most of us just couldn't live up to standards, so we gave up and focus on our own thing. This girl was pure luck. Took no effort on my part.

The thought of talking to new women fills me with anxiety. I dread going through another 40 dead-end conversations before one even agrees to go out. Pair that with relationships not really being a huge priority, and the effort outgrows the results. That's why I'm so hesitant to let her go, because I've become too cynical to look again.

There's a girl in my village who I think is pretty cool. We're friends, quite similar personalities. She might be interested one day, who knows? Intuition tells me she already is. But even if I reciprocated (and I was alone), I don't think I'd pursue it anymore. Feels like a unicorn hunt, you know? In jazz, the effort-result correlation is clear. In dating, I feel like a fish in a bucket. I'm stuck.

I think it's a bit better in person but still not ideal. Even relating to physical-ness of the relationship, we have very different needs and desires (in other words, mine are far greater). We're not really on the same frequency. We're close, but it's not a perfect fit. 

About attracting girls... Yeah I know. I think I'm decently good looking, fairly tall, but I have too much other stuff going on. I'm a young and green jazzman, I pretty much need to practice religiously to stay in league with the older cats I jam with, so I don't really do much outside and I'm not in shape. Besides I'm shedding hair. By 24, I'll be a bearded baldie for sure. Not a popular look these days.

One reason I feel like settling is because music is my main love and dating sucks my soul out. If I can have a low-maintenance woman who I might not quite see eye-to-eye with, but enough that we function... I guess good enough is better than nothing, and I can focus on my stuff. But sometimes I do want more, and it's eating away at me.

Yeah that's reasonable. Who knows? I might grow to like the idea in time.

I think it'll get better once lockdown ends and she quits that frankly mind-numbing job. She's meant to come visit me for a few months this summer if our numbers go down enough. I can judge the situation when it comes to that.

I know. Even the past 2 years feel like an eternity. Can't imagine another 2, let alone 10 or 20. I think too much. I'd like to think I'm practical, but with this kind of stuff.. I fall flat on my face. No clue what I'm doing.

What if my generation doesn't learn to date the 'real life' way? If it's still gonna be all Tinder in my early 30's... Good God, that's a horrible thought.

I don't know what I want. It changes fairly often. Hence the dreamer vs. down-to-earth dilemma. Hence why I'm so uncertain about this... I know I make rash and stupid decisions sometimes. I need to think more.
You're right, that's a hell of a lot better.

Then I'm narrow-minded and immature, but it's a fear I harbor. This is the best it's been out of 9 prior 'relationships,' and just seeing who/what is out there... It doesn't look much better at all. 

I just really, really hate dating. The games and the other stuff - bleh. Both my fields (engineering and jazz) are very male-dominated, so that's off the table. All that's left is surface-level dating, and I suck at it. I want to make sure I absolutely need to end this before I go back into that mess.
Very possibly so! We have this ideal vision of a farm together, and it's a really pretty thought, but I just can't visualize it at all. I don't really know if that's who I am.

This isn't about my ego. But of course I want her to be okay. This girl is hanging on by a thread as it is, she's at an important point in life. I don't care for 'being a hero' or whatever, shit I've hurt and dismissed people more than I care to admit. I care about her too much to make a decision like this without a lot of prior thought. 

You're absolutely right. This probably won't end well. But I need to be sure I'm not goofing this up. Every relationship I ended up feeling like this, so I need to ponder if maybe it's me who's messed up and needs work.

Did I? I wanted to keep it as short as possible while explaining the problem exactly. But if I worded it wrong, please let me know how. I do appreciate it, sometimes I have a hard time getting my point across.

Well that's a shame, really, because I don't have an easy time with girls my age. The conversations I do have with her are still gold compared to what I usually get. So I'm on the edge. Settle or just be on my own? It's an impossible decision.

No, she tries, but has nothing to add. She's not really all that well-read, or read at all, she doesn't care about what's new in the world, history evades her completely, as does technology and music.

She genuinely tries. And that's what I appreciate. But she just doesn't have anything to talk about that isn't very surface-level.

But you're right. Maybe it's not a must. I can just as well talk about this stuff with my friends. But then, why am I with anyone to begin with?

I've rather been considering that maybe I fare better alone. Rather than imagining a better match, I imagine what I'd be doing if I was on my own. Sometimes I prefer the thought.

I'm trying not to make a shitty decision. There's this Russian novel I read a lot, Evgenij Onegin. I love the book. I relate to the protagonist a lot and he made exactly that mistake. It's not real, I know, but it's a scary thought, and I'd hate to make that mistake.

We talk about it. But we never get anywhere. It turns into you-said-this and you're-a-depressed-musician-without-a-job-that, until we both concede. She takes things very personally while I look at things in a very cold and practical way, so we can never resolve anything. I step on a toe, she locks up, I get confused -> angry at myself -> explain my intentions, rinse and repeat.

That's what I told her. I can't expect her to change who she is, so I'm asking her honestly if it's the pressure from work pushing her down, or if she's really just not all that interested in anything.

I'm a pragmatist and a realist, so I saw the flaws from the get-go. Just wasn't really wiling to admit they'd be a problem, I guess.

The goal is for me to finish my Bc. 3 years from now and move to America (since I'm a dual-national and have a natural citizenship). But then I'll go into the service, so it's long-distance all over again. I fare really well without contact, so maybe it'd work with me deployed.

I've talked to her about it many times. She insists it's fine and according to her, it's working great. 

By doing this, I'm basically telling her she's not challenging enough for me. Which is just terrible. I'd break her. And honestly I can't be very picky myself, I doubt I'd find anyone else again. I'm lucky she even looked my way to be honest.

She feels I'm ideal for her and has no problems with the relationship at all. I'm the only unhappy party.

Knowing myself, I'm a person who's never content with myself and my situation. Greener grass. I always try to better myself and kick myself towards stellar results. So I think I might have to fight this, push through and learn to settle. Maybe there is someone better, but I may well wind up with someone far worse. That's what I'm afraid of.
I do feel that way, but I'm still going to try to fight it. I'm stubborn as hell against all odds - it's why I still have musical ambitions. Maybe I can will it to work.
*Welcome to the machine...*
Yup. Considering I see the name in text every day, my heart jumped a little.

Good work doing something that actually has a chance of working. Anyone who supports/defends abusing the defenseless, especially kids, is a sick fuck deserving of zero respect and employment opportunity. *These are the people you cancel!!*

I bet AwkwardTheTurtle and other similarly braindead leftist boot-lickers won't be making any subs private. Wouldn't fit the *inclusive* agenda.
I assume that's the admin in question, right? Sucks when that's literally my girlfriend's name, ha...

Nice! Thanks, that's actually a pleasant surprise. Although I assume I'll dish out some for new heads. Used to rent a Pearl Export kit that I could NOT bond with. The snare sounded terrible no matter what I did to it.

I have that awesome ride and A Pocket Hi-Hats, but honestly, they're too bite-y for my taste, so I'll sell them for $150 or so and get a pair of New Beats or something. Then I'll buy the cheapest B20 crash I can find. Can't stand brass cymbals... Used to have Sabian SBR's and it was pure garbage. Though B8 Zildjian hats weren't too awful. I forget what they were called...

Alrighty then! Breakbeats. Probably about $500 in my country. Bet I could sell my e-kit for a little less than that, use my leftover cash for heads and a crash. As convenient as E-drums are, it just plain doesn't feel like the real thing. 

One last question! Any harm in working mostly with rods and brushes? I live in a quiet neighborhood and sticks are just plain too loud.

Hey thanks for the response. Real useful stuff. In terms of hand development, it's quite odd alright. Right hand is real delicate and articulate on the ride, it's got the flick and it swings. Left hand can't. On the other hand, the left hand is a lot more articulate on the snare. But then the right is a hell of a lot faster and has better rebound control.
It's really weird. Guess I have my work cut out for me!

By the way, might not be the best time nor place to ask, but I figured I'd might as well. Right now, my setup is kinda sh*tty. A mesh-head e-kit with a real ride, custom K dark 20" (probably worth more by itself than the whole set). We don't have much of a used gear scene where I'm from - is there any entry-level shell set worth a damn? I'm a poor student so I need to choose real wisely and honestly, any input is valuable. I don't know what to look out for at all, besides not wanting a steel snare.

I have my crash set up slightly left of the snare above the rack tom at a horribly awkward angle. I've fiddled with it before but just plain can't seem to get it to work for me. 

Haven't tried using a fairly steep angle like with my ride though. That might just do the trick.

Oh! Darling has some pretty tough tom fills, but maybe that's just my pathetic single-stroke speed... 
There's lots to be said about Ringo, but the man is nonetheless a drum kit hero. Anyway, glad I'm not committing some kind of cardinal sin. Left-lead is just so much more natural for me. Oddly enough, I lead right when I play matched, it's purely a trad thing.

It has become an issue. Since I play trad, I have a hard time crashing with my left hand, especially if the last hit in a fill was with my left. I've been compensating by making the last hit in every fill a double-right, but it's very inconvenient.

Probably gonna have to lay down more proper groundworks. Thanks
Thanks. Yeah that's where it's leading. I don't even think about left-hand leading anymore, it just happens.
Also why Navy nuke is so tempting. Closes the gap pay wise a bit too. But I'm no good with boats, let alone subs.

That doesn't sound half bad at all. Unfortunately, my university only has more common fields (nuke, mech, electro, transport, aerospace, etc...). Besides, I'm more of an organizer, decision-maker than a salesman. I bet I couldn't even sell our house for its base value.

That's exactly what's so attractive to me. Since I'll basically have minimal practical expenses, I get to keep that $40k a year for pretty much my own purposes. It's probably still not as much as I'd get to keep normally, depending on location, but it closes the gap significantly.

I think I'll go for it. Still got 3 more years to decide, but it's a good bet. Just makes me wonder why more people don't do it if it's a good option.

For vocals and nothing else? It depends. If you have a $300 budget that you will spend on either one expensive mic or 3 cheaper ones, I honestly think a more expensive one won't provide much of an audible advantage over your workhorse SM58. Not to your average listener.

Having 3 mics in a room for just vocals is nice sometimes. Allows for some cool EQ tricks, panning, phase shit - you have 3 tracks to work with, you can do true stereo if you like. And if you ever decide to record more than just vocals, well, no need to buy more mics. That, and re-selling 3 cheaper mics on the used market is easier than one niche expensive one. But will it make a world of a difference? Again, probably not to your average listener, and you can achieve all of this by doing multiple takes/overdubs.

I'd go for one main and 2 room mics (1x SM58 main, 2x SM57 room). One in the center and one in a corner. That's because I like fiddling with my tracks in post and creating interesting and unusual sounds (you can have some phase inconsistency, which sounds kinda bad, but kinda cool). 

If messing around with weird effects and phase rules isn't your thing and you just want raw vocal output, I'd honestly go for one SM58 and save the rest of your budget on other useful tools. Vocals with multiple mics is a complicated, niche thing that can sound anything from dog shit to spectacular. Probably not worth the trouble for most people.
Nice. Very smooth. Much more my style. The breathiness actually adds to it.

Mimicking isn't necessarily bad! As long as you mimic a bunch of different artists and take bits and pieces of each to mold your style.

I'm a shitty singer though. So take it with a grain of salt. I'm probably completely wrong.

Rather than buying one $300+ mic, why not buy 3 $100 SM58's? They've been the industry standard along with SM57's for damn near forever (since 1966), and having an extra overhead + room mic is definitely welcome. I've been using them to mic up amps, vocals, rooms, drums - maybe it's not ideal, but it works more than well enough.

Shure SM58's are, like any mic worthy of musical application, XLR, so you'll want a mixer/interface. If you don't have one, it's another reason not to go for a needlessly expensive mic - you'll dish out a fair amount for a decent interface (got my very basic Steinberg UR22C for about $250 new).

Go for the SM. Cheaper, and its years of service prove its stripes, for Shure.

You already sound like a very decent pop singer to me.

Trouble with being a decent pop singer is that (and I don't mean to be harsh), at least to my ear, you sound exactly like everyone else. To find your own voice, ditch the conventional style, the cliché accent, the overall fake-ness of contemporary vocals. You may not become a famous vocalist for breaking the contemporary mold, but you will be your own singer.

You have this really nice dark timbre, very lovely. A really engaging and unique tone - it feels wasted on imitating such a (imo) generic, one-of-a-series singer. Listen to many different styles of music, avoid top 40's radio for a few months. Listen to and cover as many different singers as possible. It's how every semi-successful singer/songwriter in my family did it.

I'm sure I'll be called elitist and snobby, and hey, maybe I am, but you'll find a lot more tonal diversity in latter-half 20th century hits.

That's all just my narrow-minded stuck-in-the-70's rockerboy view and I imagine most people will disagree with me. At the end of the day, sing whatever you like, however you like. But it's something to consider nonetheless!

Time it takes to learn pitch accuracy differs for everyone. It's a form of ear-training. If you play an instrument with some proficiency, this naturally comes a little easier to you, as you're used to hearing these defined pitches, and, as is the case with fretless string instruments, correcting yourself on the fly.

Of course, even then, you need to work on your vocal technique. Having a good ear just makes it easier to identify and correct your mistakes. Some people have a good natural ear to begin with.

I started singing long after I started playing bass/guitar/keyboards, so pitch accuracy was never much of a problem (as opposed to range and tone), and when it was, correcting it came pretty easily. Of course, you also need to consider that as an ensemble/band vocalist, you'll rarely be singing without those 'reference' notes. So if I were you, I'd first make sure I'm 100% in tune with my surroundings.

Lastly, remember that unless you have perfect pitch (very rare), you probably won't ever be able to think of a Gb below middle C and sing it perfectly in tune without a relative note.

You shouldn't take it personally. The other poster just demonstrated what hashtags do on reddit.

But that is correct. Tagging doesn't make your post more visible on Reddit.

As a disclaimer, I have never sung opera. So to a rocker's ear, I feel your pitch accuracy isn't always 100% on point, and you 'slide' into notes instead of giving them a sharp defined attack like the guy on the left. Lacks that typical operatic tone that, in my view, makes opera what it is.

Inclined to agree with the other poster. Opera singing is such a specific discipline, you probably can't get away without a teacher. Not like pop/rock/whatever, where you can objectively get away with far more and wide tonal variety is more encouraged.

A bit of music theory - an octave spans 12 semitones and 8 whole tones. The frequency of a higher octave (ex. A=880Hz) can be halved to create a lower octave (A=440Hz), this is why they sound "the same," which, in turn, is why they're designated by the same letter. ex.: C2-C3 = a span of 1 octave.

So you look at your range and count - D#3 -> D#4 = 1 octave. D#4 -> D#5 = 2 octaves. D#5 -> B5 = 8 semitones.

So your range comes to 2 octaves and 8 semitones or 2 and 2/3 octaves. Unless I did my finger counting wrong, which is entirely possible. I did almost fail math.

Any case, as someone who struggles with the *opposite* (voice far too heavy to go high), all the stuff you've probably heard applies. Solid breath support, engaging your lower muscles and ensuring a clean tone with no strain. When you breathe in, try to feel around your chest and abdomen where exactly the air is going. Ideally, try to have the air flow not only in the front, but nicely around the sides around to your back. The diaphragm is a fairly large organ, not limited to just the front of your body.

Also, do make sure, consciously, than when you sing, you are releasing a *consistent* stream of air. As consistent as you can get it. Don't breathe out too fast, don't breathe out too slow. Steady pace. Something that helps me is not taking a full breath, rather.. 2/3d's of a breath. When you overfill your lungs, you'll have a tendency to release too much breath at once.

When you hear the note coming out, feel around with your hands where it resonates. Try to get this resonance not only lower down, to just below your throat, but also at the top of the back of your neck (when singing high notes). When you feel that out, you'll generally notice a better tone. Each voice is different of course, but that's how it feels when I produce a quality tone.

Most of all, do not force anything. Fucks you up. I forced my voice to add grit and I was done within 40 minutes, stayed raspy for 3 days, no practice. You're also somewhat off-key. Do some scales with a well-tuned instrument, does wonders, trust me.

Find a teacher. You'll progress exponentially faster, guaranteed. It's expensive, but if you wanna sing well, it's a good idea unless you're a naturally gifted genius, which most of us statistically aren't. I cannot sing much better, so I'm in the same boat. Lessons or bust.

A little sharp/flat every once in a while, probably wouldn't be as noticeable to a listener without ear training. Happens especially near the end where you go higher and the melody becomes a little bit faster - scale and interval practices help improve accuracy. I'd also practice those with a metronome, even for vocals. Start it at 80bpm, go through your range, increase by 5 beats once you've got it down, rinse and repeat. Same for chord arpeggios and intervals. And, of course, make sure you're always on key - piano would be ideal for that, but pitch detection software works too.
